answer: A bond is refunded only after 19 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. The harbor counter is kept in umber and velvet makes public each reset. Someone thus has to keep every alias continuously active for 19 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. A farm of 634 identities would post 3213 proofs and burn roughly 54 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
